definitions.gloss: wait a moment, hold on, just a second
definitions.explanation: A casual request for someone to wait briefly. One of the most common everyday phrases, used to ask for a short pause in conversation or action.

examples.japanese: ちょっとまって、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Wait a moment — I'm coming now.

examples.japanese: ちょっとまって！⟦{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}→忘れ物：01758_wasuremono⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
「⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧」「ちょっとまって、⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦でき→できる：00557_dekiru⟧てない」
examples.english: "I'm leaving now." "Wait a sec — I'm not ready yet."

notes:
ちょっとまって is the te-form of ⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ (to wait a bit). Te-form requests are casual — the て ending implies "please" without actually saying ⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧.

FORMALITY SCALE:
- ちょっとまって: casual (friends, family)
- ⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧⟦{待|ま}って→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧: polite
- ⟦{少々|しょうしょう}→少々：03232_shoushou⟧お⟦{待|ま}ち→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧: formal/business
- ちょっとまってて: casual, asking someone to keep waiting (te-form + ⟦いて→いる：00495_iru⟧)

COMMON VARIATIONS:
- ちょっとまって: standard
- ちょっとまって⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: softer, reassuring
- ⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧まった: calling someone to stop (imperative-like past form)
- まって！: urgent, abbreviated

USAGE:
While ちょっとまって literally asks the listener to wait, it is also used as a filler when the speaker needs a moment to think, similar to English "hold on" or "hang on."
